## 3. Phases: the stages, and why these

Phases become QCP phases in the Atlas process, and each step becomes a checkpoint in its
phase. A phase written from scratch has no id, so renaming it through a file later is a
delete plus a create until it has been exported once; these titles are meant to last.

| Phase | What it covers | Boundary (why the previous phase ends here) |
|---|---|---|
| {{Behov}} | {{from the request to an approved need}} | {{the hand-off to the buyer}} |

| Connectors | {{+3 −2}} | |
| Layout | {{stripped / kept}} | {{"Stripped: steps were added and moved, so Atlas lays the diagram out again and the hand arrangement is lost" / "Kept: nothing structural changed, so the arrangement survives"}} |

## 11. Importing this file

1. Save the JSON as `{{slug}}.diagram.json`.
2. **Create or open the process in Atlas Studio first.** Import goes into the process that
   is open; the file does not create one.
3. On the **Diagram** tab, choose **Import** and select the file. Atlas validates it and
   shows what will change, removals first, before anything happens.
4. **Nothing is saved by the import.** It lands on the canvas as an ordinary edit: Undo
   steps back out of it, and you press Save yourself.
5. A **published** process has no toolbar on the Diagram tab. Create a revision first.
6. Then enter §8 in Atlas: triggers, links, work files, RACI, ISO mappings, KPIs and the
   process definition. The file carries none of them.
